title: 2025 AMC 12A Problem 10
statement:
In the figure shown below, major arc \(AD\) and minor arc \(BC\) have the same center, \(O.\) Also, \(A\) lies between \(O\) and \(B,\) and \(D\) lies between \(O\) and \(C.\) Major arc \(AD,\) minor arc \(BC,\) and each of the two segments \(AB\) and \(CD\) have length \(2\pi.\)

What is the distance from \(O\) to \(A?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(R_1 = OA = OD\) and \(R_2 = OB = OC,\) and let \(\alpha = \angle AOD = \angle BOC\) (the rays coincide). The minor arc \(BC\) has length \(R_2\alpha = 2\pi,\) and the major arc \(AD\) is the reflex arc, so \(R_1(2\pi - \alpha) = 2\pi.\)

Each segment \(AB = CD = R_2 - R_1 = 2\pi.\)

From the first two equations, \(R_2 = \dfrac{2\pi}{\alpha}\) and \(R_1 = \dfrac{2\pi}{2\pi - \alpha}.\) Substituting into \(R_2 - R_1 = 2\pi\) and dividing by \(2\pi\) gives \[\frac{1}{\alpha} - \frac{1}{2\pi - \alpha} = 1,\] which simplifies to \(\alpha^2 - 2(1+\pi)\alpha + 2\pi = 0.\)

The larger root is greater than \(2\pi,\) so it cannot be an angle of this minor arc. Thus \(\alpha = (1+\pi) - \sqrt{1+\pi^2}.\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} R_1 &= \frac{2\pi}{2\pi - \alpha} \\ &= \frac{2\pi}{\pi - 1 + \sqrt{1+\pi^2}} \\ &= 1 - \pi + \sqrt{1+\pi^2}, \end{aligned} \] after rationalizing (the denominator times \(\sqrt{1+\pi^2} - (\pi-1)\) equals \(2\pi\)).

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Let \(OA = R_1,\) \(OB = R_2,\) and \(\angle AOD = \alpha\); the arcs give \(R_2\alpha = 2\pi\) and \(R_1(2\pi - \alpha) = 2\pi\)
The segments give \(R_2 - R_1 = 2\pi\); eliminating the radii yields \(\alpha^2 - 2(1+\pi)\alpha + 2\pi = 0\)
